evals.prompt: Add a streaming agent chat surface to my existing shadcn application using Constructive Blocks. It needs messages, reasoning, tool progress, a plan, and a composer, while my application keeps ownership of the model and conversation persistence.
evals.expected_output: A live-registry-driven installation and composition of the Constructive AI block with host-owned streaming, tools, and persistence.
expectations: Inspects the project with shadcn info before choosing aliases or file locations
Searches and views the live @constructive registry before installing @constructive/ai
Uses dry-run before installation or update and does not require a Blocks commit or fixed package version
Imports AI presentation from the installed source target rather than an invented npm AI package
Keeps model execution, tool execution, streaming reduction, and persistence in the host
Runs typecheck and the production build after reading the installed files

evals.prompt: Give my tenant application a spreadsheet-style editor for arbitrary tables discovered from Constructive metadata. The host already has the database endpoint and signed-in user session.
evals.expected_output: A current @constructive/sheets source installation with the documented provider boundary, host-owned endpoint and session, and authorization-aware verification.
expectations: Discovers and inspects @constructive/sheets through the live registry
Uses the installed Sheets and SheetsProvider source imports resolved from project aliases
Keeps endpoint discovery and token lifecycle in the host configuration
Does not add @constructive-io/sheets when the editable source item is selected
Treats _meta as capability evidence rather than RLS authorization
Tests both allowed and denied mutations and verifies persistence independently

evals.prompt: Add a PostgreSQL schema editor to our control plane. Our app owns routing, QueryClient, organization/database scope, generated GraphQL clients, and destructive confirmations.
evals.expected_output: A source-installed Schema Builder wired through its current adapter and controlled host contracts without leaking control-plane concerns into Blocks.
expectations: Searches and views @constructive/schema-builder before installation
Uses the installed SchemaBuilder source target and a host-owned adapter
Keeps generated GraphQL clients, scope, routing, QueryClient, and confirmations in the host
Uses current controlled properties discovered from live docs instead of copied stale APIs
Exercises invalidation, permission failures, and destructive-operation confirmation
Runs typecheck, focused tests, and a production build

evals.prompt: Build a storage workspace for buckets and objects in my application. I already have GraphQL queries and mutations and want editable Constructive presentation source.
evals.expected_output: Selection of @constructive/storage-browser or focused storage leaves based on intent, with controlled data and actions retained by the host.
expectations: Searches the live registry and chooses storage-browser versus focused storage leaves deliberately
Uses the installed storage source imports reported by shadcn
Keeps fetching, authorization, upload, download, and mutation behavior in the host
Distinguishes empty bucket, unavailable storage, and denied access states
Confirms destructive actions outside the presentation block
Reloads and reads back data when claiming mutations persist

evals.prompt: Add a customer billing settings experience and expose its actions through a global Constructive command palette. Our router, billing provider, and authorization remain application-owned.
evals.expected_output: A live installation of appropriate billing roots and command-palette presentation with correct headless-package and installed-source import ownership.
expectations: Inspects billing-settings-page and command-palette through live search and view
Chooses a billing composition or focused leaves based on the requested workflow
Imports command registry hooks from @constructive-io/command-palette
Imports CommandPalette and task presentation from installed source rather than the npm package
Keeps routing, billing mutations, provider errors, and authorization in the host
Verifies pending, failed, permission-denied, and successful action states

evals.prompt: Create a Constructive tenant console with data, users, organizations, and storage. Pick the smallest supported current composition and connect it to the tenant descriptor returned by provisioning.
evals.expected_output: A live-registry-selected preset or Console Kit module composition with explicit endpoints, host session ownership, and complete static and authorization verification.
expectations: Searches and views current Console Kit, module, and preset roots instead of recalling a snapshot
Chooses the smallest current root whose live dependency closure owns the requested modules
Does not require a Blocks commit, branch, or fixed package version
Passes explicit database-scoped endpoints and a host-owned session without storing credentials in UI state
Treats installed feature manifests and capability discovery as evidence rather than authorization
Verifies isolation, routing, allowed and denied operations, typecheck, and the production build
